purpose: Coverage inventory, not a pass report or unchanged-upstream execution claim. Every function in these three locked suites is classified; 75 reference parameter cases are not 75 candidate passes. Private Python helpers, backend variants, open metadata gaps and BSON/client representation differences are explicit.

Nonfinite BSON values and exact Decimal128 representations beyond Int64 do not match. Arbitrary Python integers outside BSON Int64 cannot travel over the wire and are rejected before mutation, not stored as Python-only values.

This monkeypatches TinyMongo's private Python numeric conversion to raise ArithmeticError. BriskDB has no such helper or hook; typed-BSON nonfinite/out-of-range matching is tested instead. This is not an unchanged injected-branch pass.

Recursive user documents/datetimes are checked across read/write result surfaces. Full listDatabases statistics still fail explicitly with code 115 under #166; only nameOnly metadata is currently available. PyMongo index metadata uses a cursor of SON documents rather than TinyMongo's indexed list of plain dictionaries. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

The same persisted BSON milliseconds are decoded with independent UTC/custom-timezone client options after reopen. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Submillisecond input changes normalize to identical BSON milliseconds, leaving update/replace modified counts zero. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

UserDict/OrderedDict materialize recursively through separate clients; mutating a returned object cannot mutate stored data or another client's result. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Both parameterized dict and UserDict aliases materialize root/nested documents as their origin types. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.
